import random

def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Find the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using the quickselect algorithm.
    
    Time Complexity: Average O(n), Worst O(n^2) due to recursion depth.
    """
    
    def partition(left, right, pivot_index):
        pivot_value = nums[pivot_index]
        # Move pivot to the end
        nums[pivot_index], nums[right] = nums[right], nums[pivot_index]
        store_index = left
        for i in range(left, right):
            if nums[i] > pivot_value:  # Change comparison for k-th largest
                nums[store_index], nums[i] = nums[i], nums[store_index]
                store_index += 1
        # Move pivot to its final place
        nums[right], nums[store_index] = nums[store_index], nums[right]
        return store_index

    def quickselect(left, right, k_smallest):
        """Return the k-th smallest element in the nums array."""
        if left == right:  # If the list contains only one element
            return nums[left]
        
        pivot_index = random.randint(left, right)
        pivot_index = partition(left, right, pivot_index)

        # The pivot is in its final sorted position
        if k_smallest == pivot_index:
            return nums[k_smallest]
        elif k_smallest < pivot_index:
            return quickselect(left, pivot_index - 1, k_smallest)
        else:
            return quickselect(pivot_index + 1, right, k_smallest)

    # Convert k to the index for k-th largest
    k_smallest = len(nums) - k
    return quickselect(0, len(nums) - 1, k_smallest)
